question_en: Jerry Johnson, CFA, has been asked to write a research report on Luke's Lockers, a leading shoe manufacturer. Johnson's wife owns 5,000 shares of Luke's stock. To comply with the Code and Standards, Johnson's most appropriate action is to:
option_a: take no action since he does not own the stock directly.
option_b: disclose this ownership of the stock in the research report.
option_c: have his wife liquidate her holdings of the stock before the research report is released.
explanation_en: Standard VI(A) Disclosure of Conflicts requires sell-side members or candidates to disclose beneficial ownership of securities they analyze. The Standard does not prohibit such beneficial ownership. For the purposes of compliance with Standard VI(A), beneficial ownership conveys the same obligations as owning the stock directly.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\8. KAPLAN MOCK-1100 MCQs\Mock Exam 5 - Answers.pdf
question_en: An investor who wants to add equity securities to her portfolio that will be relatively uncorrelated with changes in business cycles should most likely look for companies that produce:
explanation_en: Nondurable goods are goods which only have value for relatively short periods of time (such as food and gasoline). They are needed regardless of what happens in the economy, so their usage will be relatively uncorrelated to changes in business cycles. Durable goods tend to be higher value, longer lasting items with cyclical demand. Some services (e.g, travel) are discretionary and therefore cyclical while others (e.g., health care) are less so.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\8. KAPLAN MOCK-1100 MCQs\Mock Exam 5 - Answers.pdf
question_en: Which of the following statements is most accurate regarding the impact on a public company and its stakeholders from issuing additional equity rather than debt?
option_a: The company must retire debt to fund the equity issuance.
option_b: The additional shares will have an initial negative impact on earnings per share.
option_c: The cost of capital for the new equity issuance will be lower than the cost of capital for debt.
explanation_en: Issuing additional equity will increase the number of common shares outstanding, which will decrease earnings per share. A company does not have to retire debt to fund an equity issuance. The cost of capital for equity is higher than the cost of capital for debt because debt is less risky and because interest payments are tax deductible.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\8. KAPLAN MOCK-1100 MCQs\Mock Exam 5 - Answers.pdf
question_en: An investor observes that a 12-month United States Treasury bill has a quoted rate of 5.3%. If the inflation premium is 4.1%, the:
option_c: real-risk free rate of 5.3% incorporates the ination premium.
explanation_en: Nominal risk-free rates, such as the yields of U.S. Treasury bills, include the real risk- free rate and an inflation premium. If the nominal risk-free rate is 5.3% and the inflation rate is 4.1%, the real risk-free rate is approximately 5.3% – 4.1% = 1.2%.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\8. KAPLAN MOCK-1100 MCQs\Mock Exam 5 - Answers.pdf
question_en: Among all analysts who cover Saris Corporation, the consensus earnings estimate for the current period is $2.14. Lee Rutherford, CFA, believes that Saris will release earnings above the consensus number but in his published research report he estimates earnings for Saris to be $2.14 per share. In conversations with some clients Rutherford mentions his reasons for believing that the $2.14 number may be on the low side. With respect to the Code and Standards:
option_a: the conversations do not violate the Standards because the research report is the official document, and that is what Rutherford is supporting.
option_b: Rutherford is in violation of the Standards by failing to deal with clients fairly in disseminating material changes in investment recommendations.
option_c: Saris Corporation is in violation of the Standards by not disclosing material earnings information to the public.
explanation_en: Rutherford is not treating all clients fairly and is thus violating Standard III(B) Fair Dealing. If he has an opinion regarding a possible surprise earnings announcement, he should include it in his published report.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\8. KAPLAN MOCK-1100 MCQs\Mock Exam 5 - Answers.pdf
question_en: Because she has limited resources and time to devote, an economist who wishes to study the impacts of geopolitical risks should focus her time on risks with a:
explanation_en: When resources are limited, time and effort should be devoted to analysis of geopolitical risks with high probability and broad impact (potentially affecting an entire country, region, or the world).

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\8. KAPLAN MOCK-1100 MCQs\Mock Exam 5 - Answers.pdf
question_en: William Callahan, CFA, is an energy analyst. His supervisor, Nancy Dening, CFA, has recently decided to let Callahan cover a few of the firms that Dening had been covering previously. Dening gives Callahan specific instructions not to change her prior recommendation on one of these firms, Mayfield Energy. Callahan's least appropriate action is to:
option_a: tell Dening that he cannot cover Mayfield Energy under those restrictions.
option_b: perform his own independent analysis of Mayfield and reach an independent conclusion.
option_c: use ambiguous language in the report, in order to not mislead the investor while complying with his employer’s instructions.
explanation_en: In accordance with Standard I(B) Independence and Objectivity, Callahan must only issue recommendations that reflect his own independent judgment. If Dening will not permit him to do so, Callahan must refuse to cover the firm under the conditions specified.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\8. KAPLAN MOCK-1100 MCQs\Mock Exam 5 - Answers.pdf
question_en: Beena, Inc. purchases equity securities of Bear Trading for €120,000 and designates them as measured at fair value through other comprehensive income. By year-end, the securities' market value is €150,000. At year-end:
option_a: a €30,000 gain will appear on Beena’s income statement.
option_b: the investment will be valued at €120,000 on Beena’s balance sheet.
option_c: Beena’s total asset turnover ratio will be lower as a result of the €30,000 gain.
explanation_en: Because the securities will be measured at fair value on the balance sheet, assets are higher and the asset turnover ratio (sales / assets) is lower.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\8. KAPLAN MOCK-1100 MCQs\Mock Exam 5 - Answers.pdf
question_en: A company has an 11-member board of directors, an 18-member senior management team, and 650 individual shareholders. The principal-agent relationship in the company is between the:
option_a: management as the principals and the shareholders as the agents.
option_b: board of directors as the principals and the management team as the agents.
option_c: shareholders as the principals and the board and management as the agents.
explanation_en: In a corporation, the principals are the shareholders and their agents are the board of directors and senior management.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\8. KAPLAN MOCK-1100 MCQs\Mock Exam 5 - Answers.pdf
question_en: A probability tree shows that a company's expected earnings per share for the next period is $2.75. If three of the four potential outcomes used to construct the tree show a 20% probability of $2.00, a 25% probability of $2.60, and a 30% probability of $2.80, the remaining possible outcome is:
explanation_en: The probabilities must sum to 100%, so with 20%, 25%, and 30% probabilities assigned, there is 25% remaining. The calculation can be set up as follows: 20% (2.00) + 25% (2.60) + 30% (2.80) + 25% (X) = $2.75. 0.40 + 0.65 + 0.84 + 0.25X = 2.75. X = 3.44.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\8. KAPLAN MOCK-1100 MCQs\Mock Exam 5 - Answers.pdf
question_en: Which of the following is the most accurate definition of capital adequacy in the context of financial analysis of banks?
option_a: The ratio of a bank’s liabilities to its central bank reserves.
option_b: A comparison of a bank’s liquid assets to certain named liabilities.
option_c: A monetary measure of a rm’s risk as a percentage of its equity capital.
explanation_en: Capital adequacy is a monetary measure of a firm's risk as a percentage of its equity capital. The comparison of a bank's liquid assets to certain named liabilities is known as the liquid asset requirement. The ratio of a bank's liabilities to its central bank reserves refers to the bank's reserve requirements.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\8. KAPLAN MOCK-1100 MCQs\Mock Exam 5 - Answers.pdf
question_en: David Martin, CFA, recently joined Arc Financial as a portfolio manager of an emerging markets mutual fund. For the past three years, he managed an emerging markets mutual fund for Landmark Investments. Upon Martin's arrival, Arc Financial announces to existing and prospective clients, "While at Landmark Investments, Martin was the senior portfolio manager of Alpha Emerging Markets Fund. In Martin's three years as manager, this fund outperformed its benchmark each year, as documented in recent reports by Landmark." Does this statement violate the CFA Institute Standard of Professional Conduct related to performance presentation?
option_b: Yes, because the Standards prohibit showing past performance at a prior firm.
option_c: Yes, because Arc must present at least five years of Martin’s performance history.
explanation_en: Standard III(D) Performance Presentation does not prohibit showing past performance of funds managed at a previous firm as part of a performance track record if accompanied by appropriate disclosures. In this instance, Arc clearly detailed that the performance occurred while Martin was the manager of Alpha Emerging Markets Fund. A minimum 5-year performance history is not required by Standard III(D).

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\8. KAPLAN MOCK-1100 MCQs\Mock Exam 5 - Answers.pdf
question_en: If simple random sampling is used on a population with 20 data points, the probability that any individual data point is selected first in a 10 data point sample is:
explanation_en: With simple random sampling, each data point in a population has an equal probability of being selected. For a population of 50 data points, each individual data point has a 2 percent probability of being selected first. The size of the sample does not affect this probability.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\8. KAPLAN MOCK-1100 MCQs\Mock Exam 5 - Answers.pdf
question_en: Harold Fitcher asks his account manager to direct trades to Foster Brokers. Foster purchases goods and services for Fitcher at his direction. The account manager, to comply with the Standards, should inform Fitcher that he:
option_a: cannot direct the trades to Foster because of the Standard regarding soft dollars.
option_b: cannot direct trades to Foster because of his duty to seek best execution for his trades.
option_c: can direct the trades to Foster if the client tells him the goods and services will benefit the account beneficiaries.
explanation_en: Such a directed brokerage arrangement is not a violation of Standard III(A) Loyalty, Prudence, and Care because brokerage commissions are an asset of the client. As long as the client assures the manager that the goods and services will benefit the beneficiaries of the account, such an arrangement does not violate the Standards.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\8. KAPLAN MOCK-1100 MCQs\Mock Exam 5 - Answers.pdf
question_en: The audit committee of a company's board of directors is most likely responsible for:
option_a: developing the internal audit workplan for the year.
option_b: determining the annual budget for the internal audit department.
option_c: evaluating the eectiveness of the company’s internal audit department.
explanation_en: Evaluating the effectiveness of the company's internal audit department is a responsibility of the audit committee. The internal audit workplan is developed by the internal audit department itself, subject to the approval of the audit committee. The annual budget for the internal audit department is most likely to be determined by senior management.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\8. KAPLAN MOCK-1100 MCQs\Mock Exam 5 - Answers.pdf
question_en: An analyst is evaluating sample correlation coefficients to test the hypothesis that a population correlation coefficient is equal to zero. Which of the following independent actions will increase the likelihood that she will reject the hypothesis?
option_c: Decreasing the level of signicance from 10% to 5%.
explanation_en: Increasing the sample size will increase the value of the test statistic and lower the critical value. If the test statistic is greater than the critical value (as determined by the sample size and the level of significance), the hypothesis that the population correlation coefficient is zero will be rejected. Decreasing the sample correlation coefficient will decrease the test statistic, and decreasing the level of significance will increase the critical value.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\8. KAPLAN MOCK-1100 MCQs\Mock Exam 5 - Answers.pdf
question_en: For the past five years, Rafael Garcia has served as a portfolio manager for Peak Investments. Garcia accepts a position at a competing firm. Garcia is not subject to a non-compete agreement. After beginning his new job, Garcia discovers files on his home computer that contain client contact information about Peak's clients. Garcia shares this information with his new employer with the hope of bringing some of these clients over to his new firm. Garcia has:
option_a: violated the Standards because he has used information belonging to Peak Investments.
option_b: not violated any Standards because he is permitted to contact former clients after he begins the new position.
option_c: not violated any Standard because he is not subject to a non-compete agreement.
explanation_en: Garcia has violated Standard IV(A) Loyalty because the records are the property of Peak Investments. Garcia may contact former clients but most obtain their contact information from public sources.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\8. KAPLAN MOCK-1100 MCQs\Mock Exam 5 - Answers.pdf
question_en: Harriet Kedzie, CFA, manages a portfolio for a foundation. In a recent report to the foundation's directors, Kedzie explained her rationale for investing in ZYX stock as follows: "ZYX was chosen since it further diversifies the Foundation's holdings without sacrificing expected returns. In fact, ZYX's low standard deviation and high expected return ensure that the foundation will benefit from positive returns on this investment." Kedzie has most likely:
explanation_en: Kedzie has violated Standard I(C) Misrepresentation by guaranteeing that the return on ZYX stock will be positive.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\8. KAPLAN MOCK-1100 MCQs\Mock Exam 5 - Answers.pdf
question_en: One of the primary reasons why issuing debt is challenging for a start-up company is that its:
option_a: cash ow tends to be stable or growing slowly.
option_b: assets available to be used as collateral are limited.
option_c: sales and operating earnings are likely to be negative.
explanation_en: In the start-up stage of a company's life cycle, the receivables and fixed assets that are often used as collateral for debt issuances are not available yet. This makes it harder to issue debt. While operating earnings may very well be negative, sales cannot be negative. Stable cash flows (even if growing at a slower pace) are usually not found with start-up companies, and if cash flows were stable, that would make it easier to issue debt.

question_en: Robert White is a client of Song Investments, a full-service brokerage firm that produces its own investment research. A firm analyst changes her recommendation from "Buy" to "Sell" on one of the stocks that White holds in his portfolio and sends an e-mail to all firm clients, including White, informing them of the investment recommendation change. White phones John Smith, CFA, his broker at Song Investments, and asks him to buy more of all stocks that White holds in his account with the firm. Smith executes the order. With respect to fair dealing, Smith:
option_a: did not violate the Standards because his firm had already sent White an e-mail about the change in recommendation and the order is unsolicited.
option_b: did not violate the Standards because it is the analyst’s responsibility to communicate changes in her investment recommendations.
option_c: violated the Standards because he should have informed White of the change of investment recommendation from buy to sell prior to accepting the order.
explanation_en: When a client submits an order to trade in a security on which the firm has changed its recommendation, Standard III(B) Fair Dealing requires members and candidates to advise the client of the recommendation change before accepting the order. Smith should not assume White received and read the e-mail that included the change in recommendation. Notifying clients is not the analyst's responsibility.
